facts.text: Krishna Gaur is a pre-final-year Computer Science student at Bennett University, building scalable microservices and AI-backed systems with Python, TypeScript, React, and Node.js.
Krishna Gaur is pursuing a B.Tech in Computer Science Engineering at Bennett University from August 2024 to May 2028. The reported CGPA is 8.41 through the fourth semester.

Technical skills include Python, C++, JavaScript, TypeScript, SQL, PyTorch, scikit-learn, OpenCV, YOLOv8, ByteTrack, Stable-Baselines3, React, Node.js, Express, FastAPI, Docker, Redis, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Socket.IO, system design, microservices, and event-driven architecture.

As a Research Intern in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at IIT BHU from June to July 2026, Krishna benchmarked five portfolio-optimization methods across ten years of data and 100 assets, and built a differentiable PyTorch optimization layer with KKT-based backpropagation.
The research evaluation covered bull, bear, and sideways market regimes. Decision-Focused Learning reduced portfolio regret by 21 percent versus the standard-loss baseline.

The CNN-Based Underwater Image Enhancement project combines a CNN-Transformer pipeline with YOLOv8 and ByteTrack. It improved PSNR from 18.26 to 25.97 and SSIM from 0.678 to 0.878, sustaining 14.8 to 18.4 FPS across five adverse underwater conditions.

PaySure is an escrow-based payment platform with a nine-table escrow schema, milestone state machine, 24-hour auto-approval SLA, FastAPI backend, Clerk JWT authentication, HMAC-verified Razorpay payments, invoice WebSocket chat, and pytest integration coverage averaging 78 percent.

The Zomato Clone is a microservices food-delivery platform with six Node, Express, and TypeScript services, a React 19 frontend, RabbitMQ order flows, Razorpay and Stripe payments, Socket.IO updates, and four user roles. It was verified with 184 Jest and Supertest tests and a k6 result of 5.3 ms p95 latency at 100 concurrent users.
Krishna was first runner-up in the AI for Social Good Hackathon at the India AI Impact Summit 2026 among 3,312 teams, and won the GeekCode 2025 DSA contest among 300 students at Bennett University.
As Operational Head of Robogenesis at Bennett University, Krishna led a 23-member team for the inaugural DeepSight hackathon, coordinating four sponsors, a 30,000 rupee budget, and 132 participants.
